 Early voting surges in Quad Cities ahead of Election Day 
 Scott County sees in-person turnout jump 90% as Rock Island County reports more than 11,000 ballots cast 
 People in Scott County gather at the Scott County Administrative Center for early voting in the 2026 midterm elections. (KWQC) By Elisabeth Ruggiero Published : Oct. 22, 2026 at 10:00 PM CDT | Updated : 2 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google QUAD CITIES (KWQC) — Election Day is less than two weeks away, and Quad Citians are flooding the polls.
 In Scott County, early voting numbers are up about 90%, Kerri Tompkins, Scott County Auditor, said.
 By this point in 2022, she said 3,052 people had voted in person, compared with 5,785 who voted Wednesday and Thursday alone this year.
 Tompkins said because of the surge the county is doubling staff at the Bettendorf library, a popular poll this year, to keep wait times down.
 “The poll workers are doing the best that they can to get you through,” Tompkins said.
 Meanwhile mail-in ballots are down in Scott County.
 “I think people just prefer to vote in person,” Tompkins said.
 Mail-in ballots must be received by Election Day, Nov. 3, to be counted.
 Steady turnout in Rock Island Co.
 Across the Mississippi, Rock Island County is also seeing a steady stream of voters. More than 11,000 ballots have already been cast.
 Rock Island County Clerk Karen Kinney said she likes sharing the turnout numbers.
 “A lot of people are sitting on their couch thinking, I’m not going to vote; nobody else is going to vote,” Kinney said. “Well, everybody’s going to vote.”
 Kinney said a big goal of hers is to let people know the building is handicap accessible.
 “If you have a wheelchair or a walker, the doors open automatically. I mean, we make sure we’re prepared,” Kinney said.
 ILLINOIS 
 Early votes can be cast at the county building in Rock Island. Check here for days and times.
